newsitem.title: USA: EMC to unveil upgrades to storage systems.
newsitem.headline: EMC to unveil upgrades to storage systems.

text.p: EMC Corp. on Tuesday will unveil a major upgrade of its Symmetrix storage system for mainframe and network computers, a move analysts said was necessary for EMC to stay ahead of the competition.
The Hopkington, Mass.-based company said in an advisory that it was holding a news conference Tuesday in New York to make an "important technology announcement." No other details were available.
Analysts said EMC will unveil across-the-board upgrades of its disk systems with major performance improvements.

"EMC has turbocharged their subsystem," said Thomas Lahive, an analyst at International Data Corp. "The net result will be you have a higher-capacity, higher-performance product at a lower cost for the user."

Analysts said EMC's upgrade includes new models in its 3000 Series of subsystems for non-mainframe computers and its 5000 Series of subsystems for mainframe computers. The new subsystems will increase storage space with the latest in high-density drives.
EMC needs to upgrade its disk drive systems because of recent and soon-to-be announced product offerings from its disk drive competitors and some non-disk drive competitors.
"It's very important for EMC to do this," Lahive said.

Analysts said some vendors have either announced their own new storage products or have plans to. International Business Machines Corp., through its alliance with Storage Technology Corp., will unveil some storage upgrades in February. And next week, Sun Microsystems Inc. is expected to announce mainframe-like capacity storage systems.
"They have to do this stuff to stay competitve with what StorageTek and therefore IBM, Hitachi and others are doing," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial Group analyst.
